questions.question: What is Module Federation? How does it enable micro-frontends?
questions.title: Module Federation — Webpack Micro-Frontends Explained
questions.direct_answer:
What is Module Federation? How does it enable micro-frontends?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the build graph, bundler/runtime split, and deploy path), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Webpack 5 MF shares modules across separately-deployed apps at runtime; host/remote model; shared dependencies to avoid duplication.

**Classic weak answer:** Using Module Federation without planning shared deps — duplicate React versions cause hook errors.

**Senior finish:** Mention native-federation (for Vite/Angular), and the micro-frontend design trade-offs (autonomy vs coordination cost).

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Module Federation — Webpack Micro-Frontends Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is Module Federation? How does it enable micro-frontends?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Webpack 5 MF shares modules across separately-deployed apps at runtime; host/remote model; shared dependencies to avoid duplication**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Using Module Federation without planning shared deps — duplicate React versions cause hook errors**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention native-federation (for Vite/Angular), and the micro-frontend design trade-offs (autonomy vs coordination cost)**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Webpack 5 MF shares modules across separately-deployed apps at runtime; host/remote model; shared dependencies to avoid duplication
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Mental model (flowchart)
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SRC[Source TS/JS/JSX] --> TRANS[Transform (Babel / SWC)]
    TRANS --> BUNDLE[Bundler graph resolve]
    BUNDLE --> TREE[Tree-shake unused exports]
    TREE --> SPLIT[Code-split async chunks]
    SPLIT --> OUT[dist/ assets + hashes]
    OUT --> CDN[CDN / cache headers]
```

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **using Module Federation without planning shared deps — duplicate React versions cause hook errors** and what you do instead.

sections.title: Key points (memorize this list)
sections.content:
- **Headline definition** in one sentence.
- **Mechanism:** Webpack 5 MF shares modules across separately-deployed apps at runtime; host/remote model; shared dependencies to avoid duplication
- **Pitfall:** Using Module Federation without planning shared deps — duplicate React versions cause hook errors
- **Differentiator:** Mention native-federation (for Vite/Angular), and the micro-frontend design trade-offs (autonomy vs coordination cost)
- **Proof:** DevTools / Network / Performance trace, test strategy, or metric.
- **Close:** decision rule + sensible follow-up question back to the interviewer.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **Webpack 5 MF shares modules across separately-deployed apps at runtime; host/remote model; shared dependencies to avoid duplication** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Using Module Federation without planning shared deps — duplicate React versions cause hook errors** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Mention native-federation (for Vite/Angular), and the micro-frontend design trade-offs (autonomy vs coordination cost)**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).
